mergedFrom.summary: `setFreezePane` accepts any freeze position without checking existing merged blocks, retroactively splitting a block across the boundary the new paste guard protects
mergedFrom.evidence: `setFreezePane(frozenRows, frozenCols)` (sheet.ts:513-517) just assigns and persists. A user who merges A5:A6 and then freezes 5 rows ends up with a block straddling the boundary — the same renderer-hostile state `planPasteMerges` now refuses with `merge-paste-frozen`. The new guard makes the invariant explicit, but this entry point still bypasses it.

verdict.reason: `crossesFreezePane` (sheet.ts:2491) has only two call sites in the whole repository — planPasteMerges (sheet.ts:2421) and canMergeSelection (sheet.ts:4653). `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2628) pre-flights only `merge-source-split` (2659) and `merge-dest-partial` (2667), then unconditionally re-creates each travelling block at the translated anchor with `store.setMerge` / `this.merges.set` (sheet.ts:2749-2755), with no freeze-boundary test. I followed the call chain outward for an indirect guard and found none: the sole production caller is the drag-move session at view/worksheet.ts:4350, whose target comes from `toRefFromMouse`/`clampClientPointToViewport` (worksheet.ts:4243-4254, 4332-4347) with no freeze constraint, and whose entry at worksheet.ts:3958-3962 is unconditional; merging.ts has no setMerge/freeze enforcement; and `setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:513-516) neither rejects nor repairs straddling merges. Dragging a merged block so it lands across a frozen row/column therefore creates exactly the state planPasteMerges refuses and canMergeSelection forbids — an invariant break left for the renderer and later merge operations, on a normal user gesture.

mergedFrom.summary: External (TSV/HTML) pastes still write into cells covered by a destination merge, hiding the pasted values

finding.summary: Single-cell-destination exemption rests on a premise that selectRow/selectColumn/selectAllCells break, so a single-cell internal paste can still write into a hidden covered cell
finding.evidence: `planPasteMerges` returns `{pasted, replaced: []}` whenever `isCollapsedRange(destRange)` (sheet.ts:2424), justified by the comment "every path that sets `activeCell` normalizes it with `normalizeRefToAnchor`". That is false: `selectRow` sets `this.activeCell = { r: row, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3367), `selectColumn` sets `{ r: 1, c: col }` (sheet.ts:3380) and `selectAllCells` sets `{ r: 1, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3421) — none normalize. With a merge covering e.g. A2:A4 (anchor A2), clicking the row-3 header and pasting a single copied cell gives activeCell = A3 (a covered cell); the collapsed-destRange branch skips all merge handling and `setGrid` writes the value straight into A3, where it is invisible under the block and resurfaces only on unmerge. The multi-cell variant is refused by the split check, so only the single-cell path leaks.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the repo. The collapsed-destRange exemption exists at sheet.ts:2442-2444 and is justified by the comment at sheet.ts:2438-2441 claiming every activeCell setter normalizes to the merge anchor. That premise is false: selectRow (sheet.ts:3418), selectColumn (sheet.ts:3431) and selectAllCells (sheet.ts:3472) assign activeCell raw, without normalizeRefToAnchor (unlike sheet.ts:3355/3873/4713/5391). selectRow is reachable from a row-header click at view/worksheet.ts:3803, and paste is reachable at view/worksheet.ts:4939. paste computes delta from this.activeCell unnormalized (sheet.ts:2239-2242), so a single-cell internal copy yields destRange === [activeCell, activeCell]; the collapsed branch skips the getMergesIntersecting/split check (sheet.ts:2451-2456) that would otherwise refuse with 'merge-paste-partial', and setGrid (sheet.ts:991-992) writes straight to store.setGrid with no anchor normalization. Since reads normalize (getCell, sheet.ts:977-979), the pasted value lands in a covered cell: invisible under the merged block, silently lost to the user, and resurfacing on unmerge. No guard elsewhere in the clipboard path prevents this. Real correctness defect (wrong state / silently dropped user data on a normal-use path), major severity.

mergedFrom.summary: selectPastedRange now uses rangeOf(), which spreads every pasted ref into Math.min/Math.max and can throw RangeError on a large paste

finding.summary: `selectPastedRange` switched to `rangeOf`, which spreads one argument per pasted cell into `Math.min`/`Math.max` — a large paste can throw RangeError (stack overflow)
finding.evidence: The removed code walked the grid keys with an explicit loop tracking minR/maxR/minC/maxC. The replacement calls `rangeOf(grid)` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27), which does `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` with `rows.length === grid.size`. A paste of a large TSV/region (~100k+ non-empty cells, easily reachable for a 10k-row × 10-col external paste) exceeds V8's argument-spread limit and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. This happens after `store.endBatch()`, so the data is written but `paste()` rejects, leaving the caller with an unhandled rejection and no selection update. `rangeOf` is used nowhere else in src (grep `rangeOf\(`), so nothing else exercised this on paste-sized inputs.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `rangeOf` spreads one argument per grid cell into `Math.min`/`Math.max`, risking `RangeError` on a large paste. The actual implementation at packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:23-41 contains no spread at all: it folds bounds in an explicit `for (const sref of grid.keys())` loop with minR/maxR/minC/maxC accumulators and `<`/`>` comparisons. The doc comment at lines 18-21 states this was done deliberately to avoid the argument-limit RangeError on paste-sized grids. `grep 'export function rangeOf'` yields exactly one definition (coordinates.ts:23), and sheet.ts:3-20 imports `rangeOf` from that file, so there is no alternate spread-based implementation in play. `grep 'Math\.(min|max)\(\.\.\.'` over packages/sheets/src finds spreads only in formula functions (functions-math.ts:1708-1710, functions-database.ts:78/92, functions-lookup.ts:1431), none on the coordinates or paste path. The call site sheet.ts:2606 does use `rangeOf(grid)` behind a `grid.size === 0` guard at line 2604, but the argument-count-sensitive operation the finding depends on does not exist there. docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-lessons.md:40-44 confirms the spread was already replaced inside `rangeOf` so every caller gets the bound — the reviewer described an earlier state of the change, not the tree under review. With no spread, the stack-overflow and its downstream consequences (post-endBatch rejection, missing selection update) cannot occur.
